FMLA gives eligible employees 12 work weeks (rolling 12-month period) for birth/adoption/foster placement, caring for a family member with a serious health condition, the employee's own serious health condition, or military-family-related reasons.

Short Term Disability pays 60% of salary for personal medical leave, or 100% for maternity leave; the first week is covered via RealPage payroll using available PTO/sick time, and STD benefits from Unum begin on day 8.
Employees in CA, MA, NJ, NY, CT, RI, DC, CO, OR, or WA also need to file a state claim — NJ residents file family leave separately at nj.gov/labor/myleavebenefits.
RealPage keeps paying both the employee and employer share of benefit premiums during leave; missed premiums are recovered by doubling deductions after return.

steps: Coverage begins on the employee's hire date.

Electing a CDHP plan gets an HSA contribution from RealPage even without employee contributions: $25/pay period ($600/yr) for Employee Only, $50/pay period ($1,200/yr) for all other tiers.
Electing BCBS PPO makes a Medical FSA available (2026 IRS max $3,400); CDHP enrollees can use a Limited Purpose FSA (dental/vision only, same $3,400 max).
A $25/pay period wellness discount is available by completing the wellness program requirements — details at www.realpagewellness.com.
Non-exempt employees accrue PTO per pay period based on years of service (4.62 hrs/period at 0-<3 yrs, up to 7.07 hrs/period at 8+ yrs); exempt employees are on a 'Take What You Need' policy.
For retirement questions, point them to the Empower 401(k) plan and the pretax-vs-Roth contribution choice; Empower also runs monthly education webinars.
RealPage also offers a free, confidential Employee Assistance Program (EAP) through ComPsych GuidanceResources.

During: focus on behaviors and results, not personality — use STAR for praise and STAR-AR for coaching.

steps: Process your own reaction to the situation first, before involving the team.
Prepare: understand the impact on your team, and set the meeting with a clear agenda (60-90 min, ideally 8-12 participants).
Open the conversation: welcome the group, set ground rules, and acknowledge what's happening directly rather than avoiding it.
During the conversation: involve everyone, listen actively, express empathy, identify the specific challenges, and discuss solutions together.
Focus on the future: collaborate on next steps and goals, and offer to keep the conversation going rather than treating it as a one-time event.
Wrap up: summarize what was agreed, thank people for engaging, and follow up with the team afterward (including an anonymous survey if useful).
Throughout: keep referring back to the agenda, use a 'parking lot' for off-topic issues, and ask open-ended questions rather than yes/no ones.

steps: Day 1: report the NCNS to your HRBP the same day it happens, via the prescribed form or email.

Day 2: if the employee returns, serve a Notice to Explain (NTE) for the 1-day NCNS. If they remain absent, HRBP drafts a Return to Work Order (RTWO) with NTE, sent via DocuSign, work + personal email, courier, and registered mail.
Days 3-8: courier delivery window; you're expected to notify HRBP if the employee returns during this monitoring period.
Day 9: employee's deadline to respond to the NTE. If they're still NCNS, HRBP issues a 2nd RTWO with NTE via all the same channels.
The full process (RTWO through Notice of Decision) runs through Day 41 — don't try to resolve this informally past Day 1; the formal timeline needs to start immediately.

steps: Write an Incident Report with the facts and any evidence, and send it to HR and your Department Head — do this within 60 days of the incident.
Don't try to determine the penalty yourself. HR and your Department Head jointly do a preliminary evaluation to decide if a Notice to Explain (NTE) is warranted.
If an NTE is issued, the employee gets time to respond in writing: 5 calendar days if termination is a possible penalty, 3 days for a Final Written Warning, or 1 working day for any lesser warning.
Any behavior that's actively disrupting the business must stop immediately while the case is pending — that's a safety measure, not a punishment.
After the written explanation, HR and your Department Head evaluate the case together; Legal must be involved if dismissal is being recommended.

The final Notice of Decision is drafted by HR (for Final Written Warning or Dismissal) or by the Department Manager (for lower-level sanctions), then reviewed and approved up the chain — this isn't something you write or decide alone.

steps: Check the goal against the SMART criteria: Specific, Measurable, Attainable, Relevant, Time bound.
Have them start the goal with an action verb (Increase, Complete, Attain, Achieve, Reduce).
Make sure it includes a measurement (how much, how many, how much better/faster) and a due date, time frame, or frequency.
Avoid all-or-nothing goals — suggest a range (e.g. "95-100 percent") instead of a single hard threshold.
Limit it to one to three goals per major job output so the overall plan stays realistic.
Sanity check: does this goal benefit the employee, the team, and the organization? If not, help them rewrite it.

faqs.q: What's an example of a SMART goal?
faqs.a: "Decrease shipping errors by 3-5 percent by the end of the third quarter" — it has an action verb, a measurement, and a due date.

steps: Scope the change first: what's changing, why, when it needs to be done, who's impacted, and how it'll be implemented.

Use the three Change Accelerators when talking with your team: describe what's changing and why, seek their reactions and feelings, and help them find aspects of the change they can control or influence.
Expect the Emotional Cycle of Change (Uninformed Optimism to Informed Pessimism to Valley of Despair to Informed Optimism to Fulfillment) — the dip is normal, not a sign something's wrong.
Identify Change Champions, Change Agents, and Change Empaths on your team who can help others move through it.
Build a simple communication plan: what you're communicating, through what channel, and how often — and keep communicating even when there's no new update.
Partner with your HRBP for guidance specific to your team's situation.
